answer.what: the rod tore through his left frontal lobe, which plans ahead and holds back impulses, and he became impulsive and unreliable

beats.what: hook flash forward: close on Gage bent over the hole as the iron goes in under his left cheekbone and its tapered end comes out of the top of his head, lit by the blast; zoom cut back to the start
Gage leans over a drill hole in the rock cut and packs the powder with his iron, both hands on it; grit puffs from the hole on each push, a tiny spark at 1.75 s, a bigger one on 'spark'

the powder goes off: the blast drives the iron up through his head (drawn over 8 frames: in under the left cheekbone, out the top), then he is thrown back, hat knocked off; wide view of the cut, then the camera follows the iron up and pushes in on it as it turns over
low view by the landing spot: the iron slams into the ground point first in front of the camera with dust; far up the cut Gage lies by the smoking hole
back by the hole: he lies on his back; he plants both palms on the rock, then pushes himself up to sit; a worker runs in and puts his hand on his shoulder; he talks

push into his head; x ray of his head only: skull and brain; a ghost iron replays the path in under the left cheekbone and out the top; the left frontal lobe lights; chips PLANS AHEAD, HOLDS BACK IMPULSES; a round front view lens shows the iron's track left of the midline and the left frontal lobe lit
beats.source: Ratiu 2004; Van Horn 2012; AP Psychology CED unit 1

beats.what: before: sunny day, Gage points the crew to the next drill spot, plan in hand; the contractor's hand on his shoulder, he nods
after: grey day, scar and shut left eye; he jabs a finger and snaps at the contractor, turns his head away from the offered advice, drops the plan to the ground
beats.source: Harlow 1868 (profanity, impatient of advice, plans abandoned)

beats.what: dusk: Gage walks off alone; his two friends watch him go: no longer Gage

long_reason: the accident, the survival, the brain path and the before and after change all need showing for the one idea to land; 41 s with no padding (the voice runs 39.5 s)
